facts.text: Downieville was founded in late 1849 during the California Gold Rush, originally called The Forks because of its location at the confluence of the Downie and Yuba Rivers.
The town was renamed after Major William Downie, the miner who first struck gold there in September 1849.
A historic 1852 stone building houses the Downieville Museum, once a general store and now a window into 19th‑century life.
Downieville’s terrain once hosted a flume that drew water from the East Fork at Ben Pauley’s Sawmill and crossed the North Fork of the Yuba, supplying mining operations.
Downieville remains a gateway to outdoor adventures, offering white‑water rafting, snowmobiling, and skiing while preserving its gold‑rush heritage.
